title: accessiBe: an AI plug-in sold as making any website accessible, and a $1 million order
summary: accessiBe sold website owners an AI plug-in and said it would make any site meet accessibility standards. The US consumer regulator said it did not, and that reviews praising it were paid for. The company paid $1 million.
source_labels: US Federal Trade Commission (3 January 2025). FTC order requires online marketer to pay $1 million for deceptive claims that its AI product could make websites compliant with accessibility guidelines. Press release.; US Federal Trade Commission (22 April 2025). FTC approves final order requiring accessiBe to pay $1 million. Press release.

title: Air AI: the US regulator says small firms were sold “AI that replaces staff” and lost up to $250,000
summary: Air AI sold small-business owners “conversational AI” that it said could replace customer-service staff, with promises that they would earn their money back. The US consumer regulator alleges that buyers lost up to $250,000 each and that promised refunds were rarely paid. Under a proposed settlement the owners are banned from marketing business opportunities.
business: Seller of AI calling software, business coaching and licences to resell its services
period: Sales from at least February 2023; sued August 2025; proposed settlement March 2026
source_labels: US Federal Trade Commission (25 August 2025). FTC sues to stop Air AI from using deceptive claims about business growth, earnings potential, and refund guarantees. Press release.; US Federal Trade Commission (24 March 2026). Air AI and its owners will be banned from marketing business opportunities to settle FTC charges the company misled many entrepreneurs and small businesses. Press release.; US Federal Trade Commission. FTC v. Air AI Technologies, Inc. Case page with the complaint and the proposed order.

title: Air Canada: held responsible for what its website chatbot told a customer
summary: Air Canada’s website chatbot gave a customer wrong information about refunds. A Canadian tribunal ordered the airline to pay. It rejected the argument that the company was not responsible for its chatbot.
source_labels: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149. Reasons for decision, 14 February 2024. British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal.

title: Ashurst: first drafts 45–80% faster in timed trials, with lawyers still ahead on accuracy
summary: The law firm Ashurst tested generative AI with 411 of its people for five months and published the results. First drafts came 45% to 80% faster in timed tests. In a blind comparison, lawyers’ own drafts were more accurate on average, and one AI draft cited a wrong verdict.
source_labels: Ashurst (10 June 2024). Vox PopulAI: Lessons from a global law firm’s exploration of generative AI. Report.

title: Bunnings: facial recognition on every shopper in 63 stores, and what the regulator and the tribunal decided
summary: Bunnings scanned the face of every person who entered 63 of its stores to spot people it had flagged for crime or violence. The privacy regulator found that it broke the law. A tribunal later held that the chain could use the technology to fight serious retail crime, but agreed that it had not told shoppers properly and should have done a formal, documented risk assessment first.
period: November 2018 – November 2021; regulator’s decision 2024, tribunal’s decision February 2026
source_labels: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (19 November 2024). Bunnings breached Australians’ privacy with facial recognition tool. Media release on Commissioner initiated investigation into Bunnings Group Limited (Privacy) [2024] AICmr 230.; Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (2024). Bunnings determination. Fact sheet (PDF).; Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (4 February 2026). OAIC statement on Administrative Review Tribunal’s Bunnings decision. On Bunnings Group Limited and Privacy Commissioner [2026] ARTA 130.; Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (5 March 2026). Privacy Commissioner statement on Administrative Review Tribunal’s Bunnings decision.; Bunnings (4 February 2026). Bunnings statement: Response to Administrative Review Tribunal of Australia’s decision. Company statement (PDF).; Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (18 September 2025). Kmart’s use of facial recognition to tackle refund fraud unlawful, Privacy Commissioner finds. Media release.

title: Butler Snow: a firm with an AI policy, and a partner who did not follow it
summary: The firm’s policy required written approval before using ChatGPT for legal research. A partner used it without approval and filed five citations it had made up. The court removed three lawyers from the case. The firm paid for a check of 2,400 citations.
source_labels: Johnson v. Dunn, No. 2:21-cv-1701-AMM. Sanctions order, 23 July 2025. US District Court, Northern District of Alabama.

title: Commonwealth Bank of Australia cut 45 roles for a voice bot, then said they were not redundant
summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia announced that an AI voice bot would replace 45 customer-service roles. The staff union said calls were rising, not falling. A month later the bank said its assessment had been an error, that the roles were not redundant, and apologised.
source_labels: Finance Sector Union (28 July 2025). Voice bot to replace CBA jobs: urgent union meeting.; Information Age, Australian Computer Society (21 August 2025). CBA reverses AI-driven job cuts, admits ‘error’. Quotes the bank’s spokesperson and the Finance Sector Union.

title: Deloitte Australia: a government report reissued to fix wrong citations
summary: A Deloitte report for an Australian government department had to be reissued to correct citations and a summary of a court case. The corrected version disclosed the use of a generative AI tool. The report does not say AI caused the errors.
tasks: Documents, reports and paperwork; Software and IT
source_labels: Australian Government, Department of Employment and Workplace Relations. Targeted Compliance Framework Assurance Review – Final Report. Publication page and report (version updated 3 February 2026).; HR Reporter (25 November 2025). Press report on a Deloitte report for the province of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada.

title: Delphia and Global Predictions: fined for saying they used AI that they did not have
summary: Two investment advisers advertised AI they did not have. One said its AI learned from client data. The other called itself the first regulated AI financial advisor. The US securities regulator fined them $225,000 and $175,000.
country: United States (the firms are based in Toronto and San Francisco)
source_labels: US Securities and Exchange Commission (18 March 2024). SEC charges two investment advisers with making false and misleading statements about their use of artificial intelligence. Press release 2024-36.

title: Victoria’s child protection service: a worker put case details into ChatGPT, and the regulator ordered the tools blocked
summary: A child protection worker typed personal details of a family into ChatGPT to draft a court report. The report contained errors. The privacy regulator found the department had no rules, no training and no technical limits for such tools, and ordered it to block them.
company: Department of Families, Fairness and Housing (Victoria)
business: State government department, including child protection
source_labels: Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner (September 2024). Investigation into the use of ChatGPT by a Child Protection worker. Report, with the compliance notice and the department’s response.

title: DoNotPay: a “robot lawyer” that was never tested against a lawyer
summary: DoNotPay told customers its AI could do the work of a lawyer. The US consumer regulator said the company had never tested whether that was true and employed no lawyers to check. It paid $193,000 and had to tell past subscribers about the limits.
business: Online subscription service for legal documents
source_labels: US Federal Trade Commission (25 September 2024). FTC announces crackdown on deceptive AI claims and schemes. Press release.; US Federal Trade Commission (11 February 2025). FTC finalizes order with DoNotPay that prohibits deceptive “AI lawyer” claims, imposes monetary relief, and requires notice to past subscribers. Press release.

title: Duolingo: 148 new language courses in about a year, after 12 years for the first 100
summary: Duolingo replaced a slow, manual way of writing language courses with one built around AI. It launched 148 new courses in under a year, after taking about 12 years over its first 100. The same week, its chief executive told all staff what “AI-first” would mean for contractors, hiring and headcount.
source_labels: Duolingo (30 April 2025). Duolingo Launches 148 New Language Courses. Press release, as carried by Nasdaq.; Duolingo (1 May 2025). First quarter 2025 shareholder letter, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.; Duolingo (28 April 2025). All-hands email from chief executive Luis von Ahn, published by the company on LinkedIn.; Duolingo (28 February 2025). Annual report for 2024 (Form 10-K), filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Source of the employee count.

title: eBay: machine translation raised cross-border sales by about 11%
summary: eBay began translating search queries and listing titles for Spanish-speaking buyers. A peer-reviewed study found that US exports to those buyers on eBay rose by 10.9%. It is one of the few AI results in retail measured by outside researchers.
country: United States sellers, buyers in Spanish-speaking Latin America
source_labels: Brynjolfsson, Hui and Liu (2019). Does Machine Translation Affect International Trade? Evidence from a Large Digital Platform. Management Science, 65(12), 5449–5460.; Brynjolfsson, Hui and Liu (2018). The same study as NBER Working Paper 24917 (earlier version, free to read).

title: EIST: a six-person metalworking shop cut quoting time from two hours to ten minutes
summary: A metalworking shop with five employees and an owner used AI to price custom parts from 3D files and its own production history. A quote that could take two hours now takes about ten minutes. Most of the project was spent cleaning the firm’s data, and the owner still checks every quote.
business: Maker of custom sheet-metal parts and industrial equipment
period: A project of six to eight months, published June 2026
source_labels: France Num (9 June 2026). Comment une TPE industrielle utilise l’IA pour réaliser un devis en 10 minutes au lieu de 2 heures. Case page, in French.

title: Fiverr cut about 250 jobs to become “an AI-first company” and promised investors a higher margin
summary: Fiverr let go about 30% of its staff and told investors it would reach a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026, a year early. The cut is on record in its annual report. The margin promise is not: by mid-2026 its revenue was falling and its own forecasts pointed lower.
tasks: Customer service and support; Security, fraud and monitoring
source_labels: Fiverr International (15 September 2025). Form 6-K: reduction in force of approximately 250 team members, with the letter to shareholders and the chief executive’s letter to staff (Exhibit 99.1). Filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.; Fiverr International (19 February 2025). Annual report for 2024 (Form 20-F). Source of the 2024 employee count.; Fiverr International (12 March 2026). Annual report for 2025 (Form 20-F). Source of the 2025 employee count, the restructuring cost and the contractor spending.; Fiverr International (5 November 2025). Third-quarter 2025 results. Press release, Form 6-K.; Fiverr International (18 February 2026). Fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results. Press release, Form 6-K.; Fiverr International (29 April 2026). First-quarter 2026 results. Press release, Form 6-K.; Fiverr International (29 July 2026). Second-quarter 2026 results. Press release, Form 6-K.

title: Garfield.Law: a regulator authorised an AI-run law firm for small debt claims, with limits
summary: The regulator of solicitors in England and Wales authorised its first law firm that delivers legal services through AI. It helps businesses recover unpaid debts through the small-claims court. The regulator set limits: the AI may not propose case law, takes no step the client has not approved, and named solicitors stay accountable.
business: Law firm that uses AI to help businesses recover unpaid debts through the small-claims court
period: Authorised May 2025; first trial reported June 2026
source_labels: Solicitors Regulation Authority (6 May 2025). SRA approves first AI-driven law firm. Announcement.; Scottish Legal News (23 June 2026). England: AI law firm wins first court case after landmark trial.

title: Gilberts: a smaller audit firm started with the AI in its existing tools and two firm rules
summary: A smaller UK audit and accountancy firm began with the AI features in tools it already had, on low-risk internal tasks. A partner reports that summarising a long document now takes 10 to 15 minutes where it took 45. The firm bars client data from public AI tools and treats every AI output as a first draft.
source_labels: Luke Parker, Partner, Gilberts Chartered Accountants (July 2025). AI: a smaller firm’s perspective. Audit & Beyond, ICAEW Audit and Assurance Faculty.

title: Herges: an AI model estimated production times five times more accurately than the firm’s experts
summary: A family-owned steel fabricator prices one-off jobs from its experts’ estimates of how long the work will take. A public support centre helped it record real times and train an AI model on them. The model’s estimates were five times closer to the real figure than the experts’ own.
business: Family-owned maker of welded steel and sheet-metal constructions, mostly one-off
source_labels: Mittelstand-Digital Zentrum Saarbrücken (March 2026). KI-gestützte Datenanalyse zur Prozesszeitenermittlung. Project report, in German.

title: Hitachi Energy: an AI model pointed to the two production steps that were spoiling chips
summary: Researchers trained an AI model on the production records of a chip plant and asked it which process steps did most to spoil chips. Engineers tested its two suggestions on a live batch, and losses fell by 21.7%. On a second product the same method cut losses by 51.3%. The plant’s usual analysis had missed both causes.
business: Maker of power semiconductors; at the time of the study the plant belonged to Hitachi ABB Power Grids
period: Data to April 2019, rollout February – August 2020, published 2021
source_labels: Senoner, Netland and Feuerriegel (2022). Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence to Improve Process Quality: Evidence from Semiconductor Manufacturing. Management Science, 68(8), 5704–5723.; The same paper, free to read in the ETH Zurich Research Collection.; ETH Zurich (15 December 2021). Improving quality through artificial intelligence. News article naming the plant as Hitachi Energy, Lenzburg.

title: HMRC gave 3,000 Copilot licences at random: about an hour a week saved, by staff estimate
summary: The UK tax authority picked 3,000 staff at random and gave them an AI assistant inside their office software for three months. Most used it and liked it. Staff estimated it saved about an hour a week, and the authority cut self-reported estimates to allow for keen users answering more often.
source_labels: HM Revenue & Customs (9 July 2026). Evaluating the impact of Microsoft Copilot in HMRC. Evaluation report, phase III trial.; UK Government Digital Service (2 June 2025). Microsoft 365 Copilot experiment: cross-government findings report. The wider trial with about 20,000 staff.

title: Klarna: AI cut spending on outside marketing suppliers by a quarter
summary: Klarna reported that AI tools let it spend 25% less on outside marketing suppliers while running more campaigns. For agencies, it is a client saying in public which work it has taken in-house.
source_labels: Klarna (28 May 2024). AI helps Klarna cut marketing agency spend by 25% and run more campaigns. Press release.

title: Klarna: an AI assistant took two-thirds of support chats, then the company hired people again
summary: Klarna reported large savings from an AI support assistant. About a year later its chief executive said the company had judged the work too much on cost, and it began hiring human agents again. The AI assistant stayed.
source_labels: Klarna (27 February 2024). Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month. Press release.; Klarna (19 May 2025). First-quarter 2025 results. Press release.; Customer Experience Dive (9 May 2025). Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service. Reports the chief executive’s interview with Bloomberg and a statement from Klarna.; Customer Experience Dive (20 November 2025). Klarna says its AI agent is doing the work of 853 employees. Reports Klarna’s third-quarter 2025 earnings call.; Klarna Group plc. Fourth-quarter 2025 results. Press release.

title: Levidow, Levidow & Oberman: fined after filing court papers with cases ChatGPT made up
summary: A lawyer used ChatGPT for legal research and filed six court decisions that did not exist. The court fined the firm and two of its lawyers. The judge said using AI was not the problem. Not checking was.
country: United States (federal court in New York)
source_labels: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461 (PKC). Opinion and Order on Sanctions, 22 June 2023. US District Court, Southern District of New York.

title: META-Regalbau: sensors and AI analysis of order picking paid back in about a year
summary: A shelving manufacturer with about 300 employees had staff wear small sensors so that AI could analyse how orders are picked in its warehouse. The findings shaped the layout of a new warehouse and save about €22,000 a year. Managers, the works council and all staff were told the purpose from the start.
business: Maker of shelving and racking systems
source_labels: Plattform Lernende Systeme (August 2021). KI im Mittelstand: Potenziale erkennen, Voraussetzungen schaffen, Transformation meistern. Report, in German, with a section on this company.

title: Milkforbubs: a small online shop put a ready-made chatbot on customer questions
summary: A small online shop in Singapore bought a ready-made AI chatbot to answer customers. The team loaded it with common questions, trained staff, and keeps correcting its answers. The founder estimates the team spends 30% less time on customer questions.
business: Online shop for foods and accessories for breastfeeding mothers
source_labels: Infocomm Media Development Authority, Singapore (9 September 2025). Happier customers and 30% time savings for Milkforbubs. Article.

title: Ministry of Clean: a cleaning company moved its customers from spreadsheets to a CRM with AI built in
summary: A Singapore cleaning company kept its customer list in spreadsheets. It moved to ready-made customer-management software that drafts replies and suggests the next step with each lead. The company reports replies in 10 minutes where they took an hour, and 30% more sales revenue.
business: Cleaning services and disinfecting coatings for homes and businesses
tasks: Customer service and support; Sales and the online shop
source_labels: Infocomm Media Development Authority, Singapore (October 2025). SMEs’ Digital Transformation Success Stories. Annex B to the press release for SMEs Go Digital Day.; Infocomm Media Development Authority, Singapore (October 2025). Smarter, Simpler, Safer: Singapore Offers Stronger Support to Help Local SMEs Go Digital with Confidence. Press release.

title: Morgan & Morgan: eight made-up cases from the firm’s own AI tool, signed by three lawyers
summary: A lawyer asked his firm’s own AI tool to add case law to a court filing. Eight of the nine cases it cited did not exist. Two other lawyers signed without reading. The firm had trained staff, and it then added a warning inside the tool.
source_labels: Wadsworth v. Walmart Inc., No. 2:23-cv-118-KHR. Order on Sanctions and Other Disciplinary Action, 24 February 2025. US District Court, District of Wyoming.; Morgan & Morgan. About us (the firm’s own description of its size).

title: NSW Reconstruction Authority: a temporary worker uploaded data on 2,031 people to ChatGPT
summary: A temporary staff member uploaded a spreadsheet of flood-recovery applicants to ChatGPT, which the agency had not approved. It held personal and health details of 2,031 people. The agency then wrote AI guidance, tightened training and blocked such uploads.
business: State government agency for disaster recovery
source_labels: NSW Reconstruction Authority. Resilient Homes Program data breach. Public notice and questions and answers (updated 26 March 2026).

title: Presto Automation: the US regulator found most “AI” drive-through orders needed a person
summary: Presto sold restaurants a voice AI for drive-through orders and told investors it eliminated human order-taking. The US securities regulator found that people working off site, mainly in the Philippines and India, entered the vast majority of orders. Presto settled without admitting or denying the findings.
period: Statements made November 2021 – May 2023, order January 2025
source_labels: US Securities and Exchange Commission (14 January 2025). In the Matter of Presto Automation Inc. Announcement of settled charges, File No. 3-22413.; US Securities and Exchange Commission (14 January 2025). Order instituting cease-and-desist proceedings, Release No. 33-11352.

title: Primus Solicitors: 18 court citations that did not exist, taken from a client’s AI research
summary: A solicitor at a small law firm filed a statement with 45 case citations. Eighteen of the cases did not exist. His client had produced the research with public AI tools, and nobody at the firm checked it. The court referred him to his regulator.
source_labels: R (Ayinde) v London Borough of Haringey and Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin). Judgment of 6 June 2025. High Court of England and Wales, Divisional Court.; Companies House. Primus Solicitors Limited (company number 10999760). Filing history, accounts for the year to 30 April 2025.

title: Procter & Gamble: one person with AI matched a two-person team without it
summary: Researchers ran an experiment with 776 Procter & Gamble staff on real product-development tasks. People working alone with AI produced ideas rated as highly as those of two-person teams without AI, and did it faster.
source_labels: Dell’Acqua, Ayoubi, Lifshitz, Sadun, Mollick, Mollick, Han, Goldman, Nair, Taub and Lakhani (2025). The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise. NBER Working Paper 33641.

title: PSG Global Solutions: AI ran the job interviews, and people made the hiring decisions
summary: A recruitment firm let an AI voice agent carry out job interviews, while its human recruiters kept every hiring decision. In a randomised study of 70,884 applications, people interviewed by the AI were 12% more likely to get an offer and more likely to stay in the job.
business: Recruitment outsourcing firm, part of Teleperformance
source_labels: Jabarian and Henkel (2026). Voice AI in Firms: A Natural Field Experiment on Automated Job Interviews. Working paper, arXiv 2607.28222.

title: Rite Aid: banned from facial recognition for five years after buying it without testing it
summary: Rite Aid used facial recognition to spot suspected shoplifters. The US consumer regulator said the chain never asked its vendors how accurate the system was, never tested it and did not train staff. Shoppers were wrongly accused. The chain was banned from the technology for five years.
source_labels: US Federal Trade Commission (19 December 2023). Rite Aid banned from using AI facial recognition after FTC says retailer deployed technology without reasonable safeguards. Press release.

title: Rue La La: machine-learning price recommendations raised revenue by about 10% in a test
summary: Rue La La, an online fashion retailer, had a tool built that predicts demand for products it has never sold and recommends a price for each. In a five-month test, researchers estimated that revenue on the tested products rose by 9.7%. The retailer set firm limits on what the tool could do before it let it near a price.
business: Online retailer selling designer clothing and accessories in short sales events
source_labels: Ferreira, Lee and Simchi-Levi (2016). Analytics for an Online Retailer: Demand Forecasting and Price Optimization. Manufacturing & Service Operations Management, 18(1), 69–88.; The same paper, free to read in Harvard’s open-access repository.

title: SAM: a two-person advisory firm cut the paperwork on each client file from six hours to two and a half
summary: A two-person firm that advises clients on retirement turned each client file into a fixed sequence of steps and gave the routine ones to AI. Administrative time per file fell from about six hours to two and a half. Set-up cost about €3,000 and 60 hours, and the adviser still approves important letters.
business: Retirement advisory firm for individuals and business owners
period: Six months of use, published May 2026
source_labels: France Num (26 May 2026). Dans les Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, une entreprise de conseil retraite déploie des agents IA pour automatiser le traitement de ses dossiers. Case page, in French.

title: Siemens: inspectors caught more defects when the AI showed what it had seen
summary: Researchers gave 48 inspectors at a Siemens electronics factory an AI aid for checking circuit boards. Half saw only the AI’s score. Half also saw a picture marking where the AI had found a problem. The second group caught more defects, and most of them did better than the AI working alone.
business: Industrial manufacturer; the study was run at its electronics factory in Zug
source_labels: Senoner, Schallmoser, Kratzwald, Feuerriegel and Netland (2024). Explainable AI improves task performance in human–AI collaboration. Scientific Reports, 14, 31150.

title: Temple & Webster: an online furniture retailer with about 200 staff put AI into customer care first
summary: Temple & Webster sells furniture online with about 200 employees. It reports that AI and automation handle 80% of customer contacts in whole or in part, and that customer care now costs over 60% less as a share of revenue. It then set up central approval, training and a contact person for AI in every department.
business: Online retailer of furniture and homewares
tasks: Customer service and support; Sales and the online shop
source_labels: Temple & Webster Group (29 September 2026). Annual Report 2026. Filed with the Australian Securities Exchange.; Temple & Webster Group (14 August 2025). Appendix 4E and annual report for the year to 30 June 2025. Filed with the Australian Securities Exchange.

title: UK Department for Business and Trade: 1,000 Copilot licences, satisfied users, no proven productivity gain
summary: A UK government department gave 1,000 staff an AI assistant inside the office software they already used, and measured the result. Most users were satisfied and writing tasks went faster. Some tasks went slower or came out worse, and the department found no evidence of higher productivity.
company: UK Department for Business and Trade
source_labels: UK Department for Business and Trade (August 2025). The evaluation of the M365 Copilot pilot in the Department for Business and Trade. Report.; UK Government Digital Service (2 June 2025). Microsoft 365 Copilot experiment: cross-government findings report. The wider trial this pilot was part of.; HM Revenue & Customs (9 July 2026). Evaluating the impact of Microsoft Copilot in HMRC. Phase III trial evaluation report.

title: Walmart: generative AI used to fix 850 million pieces of product data
summary: Walmart told investors it used generative AI to create or improve more than 850 million pieces of product data. The task is narrow, repetitive and easy to check, which is where AI tends to work.
source_labels: Walmart Inc. (15 August 2024). Q2 fiscal year 2025 earnings call. Corrected transcript, published on Walmart’s investor site.

title: Workado: an AI detector sold as 98% accurate that tested at 53%
summary: Workado sold a tool that claims to tell AI-written text from human writing, and advertised it as 98% accurate. The US consumer regulator said independent testing put it at 53% on general text. Buyers had only the vendor’s word.
business: Software vendor: AI writing and detection tools
source_labels: US Federal Trade Commission (28 April 2025). FTC order requires Workado to back up artificial intelligence detection claims. Press release.; US Federal Trade Commission (28 August 2025). FTC approves final order against Workado, LLC. Press release.

title: WPP: £300 million a year on an AI platform, and revenue still fell
summary: WPP, one of the largest advertising groups, invested heavily in its own AI platform and reported wide use by staff. Its revenue still fell in 2025. Investing in AI did not, on its own, protect an agency’s income.
source_labels: WPP plc (2025). Annual report on Form 20-F for the year ended 31 December 2024. US Securities and Exchange Commission.; WPP plc (30 October 2025). Third Quarter Trading Update 2025.

title: Zillow Offers: home-price forecasts missed, and Zillow shut its home-buying business
summary: Zillow bought homes to resell, at prices set with its own algorithms and in-person checks. In 2021 its forecasts of resale prices missed by far more than it had planned for. It wrote down $407.9 million of homes, shut the business and cut about a quarter of its staff. Zillow named labour and supply problems as well as the forecasts.
business: Online real estate marketplace; Zillow Offers bought and resold homes
source_labels: Zillow Group (2 November 2021). Q3 2021 shareholder letter. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.3, US Securities and Exchange Commission.; Zillow Group (2 November 2021). Zillow Group Reports Third-Quarter 2021 Financial Results & Shares Plan to Wind Down Zillow Offers Operations. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1.; Zillow Group (10 February 2022). Q4 2021 shareholder letter. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.3.; Zillow Group (10 February 2022). Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2021.
